beats.text: At twenty, a girl walked in a procession, and her life changed.
Marguerite Bourgeoys was born in Troyes, in 1620.
beats.scene: A seventeenth-century French town seen from a hillside at dawn: steep crooked half-timbered houses packed along a winding river, a great Gothic cathedral with a single unfinished tower rising over the rooftops, mist in the valley, a hard low light from one side. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: Her mother died before she turned twenty.
She joined a sodality that taught poor girls.
beats.scene: A bare seventeenth-century French schoolroom of one long table and rows of plain wooden benches, empty, a high window throwing a hard shaft of light across the floorboards, a slate and a small crucifix on the wall, drifting dust. No people.

beats.text: Then came a Rosary procession, on the seventh of October, 1640.
She felt called to give her life to God, and did not yet know how.
That call would take her across an ocean.
beats.scene: A lone sailing ship of the seventeenth century on a vast dark sea under a heavy sky, seen from far away, one hard shaft of light falling on its sails, towering waves, mist on the horizon. No people.

beats.text: For years she went on teaching, and waited.
